How Things Are Going Now

Operational performance over the last three consecutive quarters (Q4 2025 revenue of $19.1B, Q1 2026 revenue of $17.4B, and Q2 2026 record revenue of $20.5B, up 24% YoY) demonstrates Caterpillar executing at peak capacity. Annualized Q2 run-rate revenue stands at $82,172.0M. Consolidated gross margins expanded to 37.8% while GAAP operating margin reached 20.9% (adjusted to 21.9%), driven by $3.1B in higher sales volume and $595M in equipment price realization. Total order backlog reached a record $72.0B, with power generation retail sales surging 72% YoY on relentless hyperscaler demand for data center backup power.

Segment results show broad momentum: Construction Industries generated $8.30B in Q2 sales (+35% YoY) on strong North American non-residential demand, while Power & Energy contributed $8.20B (+17% YoY) with segment operating margins expanding to 24.6%. Pricing realization continues to outpace manufacturing inflation, supported by a $392M IEEPA tariff refund in Q2 2026. Management has raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to mid-to-high teens growth and expects enterprise cash flow at the top end of targets.

Capital allocation across the recent quarters has been aggressive yet controversial. Deployments included $2.2B in Q2 2026 ($1.5B buybacks, $0.7B dividends) following $5.7B deployed in Q1 2026 ($5.0B buybacks, $0.7B dividends), reducing share count to 480.0M. However, with net debt standing at \(-31,552M (\)-65.73/share), repurchasing shares at 43.9x Owner Earnings consumes liquidity that would create greater intrinsic value if directed toward balance sheet deleveraging.
